title: Allowance dot states
slide_intent: Teach designers to distinguish balance, availability and pending action in one visual vocabulary so a viewer can tell what a key currently permits.
strategic_value: Halfkey can carry a recognizable key from a compact wallet row to a weekly poster while keeping an empty allowance distinct from a paused key or a request awaiting approval.
demonstration: Five states of the $40 key retain the disc footprint and vary fill, dot area or a separate black indicator. Below them, the same device appears at six sizes and across four poster treatments.
practical_value: A designer can choose the locked outline for a paused key, the black indicator for a waiting ask, and a simplified twelve-dot drawing at 24 px or below.

content_islands.name: Running header
content_islands.spec: Retain the small brand-book header, title and folio above the pale dotted field.

content_islands.name: State comparison
content_islands.spec: Arrange five equal columns labeled Full, Spending, Empty, Locked and Ask. Show a full $40 disc, the partly depleted $12.40 disc, the spent pinpoints, empty outlined places and a full disc with one black ask dot. Put a status line and a brief explanation under each.

content_islands.name: Size range
content_islands.spec: Place the six scale specimens at lower left, labeled 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 and 96 px. Put the small-size redraw rule underneath and finish with a compact Weekly SOL buy row that pairs the symbol with its balance.

content_islands.name: Weekly poster series
content_islands.spec: Place four same-size posters side by side at lower right. Use blue, ink, white and pale backgrounds, a key drawing and a single result or status on each. Keep the comparisons close enough to see how each key state changes the composition.
